Trailing P/E of 23.65× sits within the IT sector benchmark range of 22–30×, grading FAIR; however, forward P/E of 17.21× falls significantly below the sector lower bound and the EV/EBITDA of 15.15× is at a 35% discount to the broad-market median (23.3×), and with the stock at just 7.4% of its 52-week range (near lows), risk/reward tilts incrementally toward cheap — primary yardstick used is P/E + EV/EBITDA given the IT services capital-light model. The biggest risk is that a 73.9% US revenue concentration faces the active RISK_OFF macro headwind (IT sector macro underweight, rising US yields), while an anomalously high D/E of 9.58× — atypical for an IT peer and possibly inflated by Ind AS 116 leases plus the pending €160M Randstad acquisition — adds balance-sheet uncertainty that is not yet resolved.

Newgen is a mid-cap Indian software product company that sells low-code and AI-led process automation platforms (NewgenONE), mainly to banks, insurers and governments. It is not a headcount-driven services firm. Q2FY27 revenue was ₹422 cr (+5.0% YoY) and PAT was ₹87 cr (+6.0% YoY, 20.6% margin). Headline growth has slowed from +11.2% in Q1FY27, so the pre-computed 'accelerating' label is wrong because the table is ordered newest-first. Underneath, quality is better: annuity revenue grew 15% to ₹268 cr (63.5% of revenue), SaaS grew 36% (down from 40%) and subscription grew 18% (down from 21%), while lumpy licence and implementation revenue dragged the total. On the IT yardstick of trailing P/E, the stock trades at 22.6×, the bottom of the 22–30× IT band, with forward P/E of 17.1×, EV/EBITDA of 14.8× (P25 vs the broad market) and price at 15.7% of its 52-week range, so I grade it fair-to-cheap and call it fair. The biggest risk is that headline growth stays in single digits while the founder CMD, Diwakar Nigam, remains unavailable due to ill-health. That combines with next-FY EPS estimate cuts (-2.5% over 90 days) and middling cash conversion (CFO/PAT 0.72×).

fundamental.thesis: Sagility is a mid-cap healthcare outsourcing company. About 90% of revenue comes from US health insurers (payers) and about 10% from hospitals and other providers. It is tagged IT here, but its demand comes from US healthcare operations, not tech spending. In Q2FY27 revenue was ₹2,032 cr, up 22.5% YoY, and PAT was ₹284 cr, up 13.3%. Growth has slowed from +35.7% (Q3FY26) to +29.1% (FY26) to +25.0% (H1) to +22.5%, and constant-currency growth is only about 12%, so roughly half the headline growth comes from the weak rupee. Reported PAT margin fell to 14.0% from 15.1% a year ago, and adjusted PAT grew only 8.1% even though adjusted EBITDA margin reached a six-quarter high of 26.3%. On valuation, using P/E and EV/EBITDA, the trailing P/E of 21.5x is below the IT sector's 22–30x range and sits at about the 24th percentile of the broad market (there are no close peers in the universe). EV/EBITDA is 11.4x, forward P/E is 15.4x, and cash conversion is strong (CFO/PAT 1.27x), so the stock looks cheap. The biggest risk is client concentration: the top 3 clients are 60% of revenue and the top 10 are 84%, and voluntary attrition is high at 25.7%. Losing or repricing a single large client could hurt badly. The yfinance dividend yield (44%) and debt/equity (11.5) figures look like unit errors, so I ignored them.

fundamental.thesis: Sonata Software is a mid-cap IT services company focused on platform-led modernisation (MASC stack) with growing cloud/AI partnerships — the September 2026 five-year AWS SCA signals enterprise positioning, and appointment of a Chief AI Officer suggests management repositioning toward AI-native delivery. At a trailing P/E of 15.57× against the IT sector median of 22–30×, the stock screens unambiguously cheap (P15 vs broad market, -55.7% vs median) and forward P/E of 12.69× implies the market has already priced in some earnings recovery — but the deep discount is likely deserved given negative CC growth, high debt/equity of 37.96, and 90-day EPS estimate cuts of -5.4% that signal sell-side conviction in the deterioration. The biggest fundamental risk is that AI-driven budget deflation in Sonata's enterprise client base makes negative CC growth structural rather than cyclical, converting apparent valuation cheapness into a sustained earnings-decline trap — data quality is further constrained by filing staleness (latest indexed extraction is 9M FY25, making Q1 FY27 performance unconfirmed from official sources).

fundamental.thesis: Tata Elxsi is a Tata Group engineering R&D services company specialising in embedded systems design for automotive, media & entertainment, and healthcare verticals — a niche deep-tech services player distinct from commodity IT outsourcers, with a strong domestic and global client base in high-complexity design programmes. Revenue growth has inflected sharply from a -3.9% trough in Q2FY26 to +14.7% YoY in H1FY27 (₹2,077 cr), with PAT rising +13.9% to ₹341 cr and PAT margin holding steady at 16.4%; the System Integration segment contributed 28.9% YoY growth, signalling service diversification — however, EBITDA margin has contracted ~290 bps from its peak of 28.1% (Q3FY26) to 25.2% (H1FY27), driven by New Labour Code wage provisions and rising employee benefits costs. Trailing P/E of 40.78× is above the IT sector benchmark upper bound of 30× (expensive on that metric alone), but the forward P/E collapses to 26.22× — within the 22–30× sector range, confirming earnings recovery is priced in — and peer-rank analysis places TATAELXSI at P60 on both trailing and forward P/E (fairly valued per the ≥P75 expensive threshold); at 6.7% of its 52-week range the stock appears sentiment-oversold relative to an improving earnings trajectory, consistent with the FY26 exceptional charge now cycling out of the base. The primary risk is sustained EBITDA margin compression from structural wage inflation and New Labour Code costs, amplified by a persistent negative EPS revision trend (-0.9% over 90 days, -1.2% next-FY) that historically flags further analyst downgrades ahead, and a long-run AI-driven structural threat to engineering services demand that the sector card explicitly flags as unproven in revenue terms.

fundamental.thesis: Zensar Technologies (RPG Group) is a mid-cap IT services provider focused on cloud infrastructure, data analytics, and digital transformation, with Cloud & Security now the fastest-growing segment at +16.8% YoY — outperforming tier-1 peers that are near-flat in constant currency. At a trailing P/E of 12.6×, ZENSARTECH is at P10 in the broad market and roughly half the IT sector median of 22–30×, with EV/EBITDA of 8.2× equally discounted (P7 broad-market rank) — the valuation is unambiguously cheap, but the stock sitting at 0.9% of its 52-week range signals the market is pricing in sustained deterioration rather than a mispricing gap. The primary risk is that PAT margin erosion continues — elevated subcontracting, AI-driven pricing pressure on legacy services, anomalously high D/E of 1.68 for an asset-light IT business, and 90-day EPS revisions of -3.8% all point toward a value trap rather than a mean-reversion opportunity.

Adani Energy Solutions is India's largest private power-transmission company, with about 30% market share, plus the Mumbai distribution business and a fast-growing smart-meter platform, which together form a regulated-asset compounder funded by heavy borrowing. H1 FY27 revenue rose 47.5% YoY to ₹19,787 cr and PAT rose 137% to ₹2,600 cr; backing out Q1 (₹9,711 cr revenue, ₹1,149 cr PAT) gives an implied Q2 of about ₹10,076 cr revenue (about +53% YoY) and ₹1,451 cr PAT (about 14.4% margin), so growth is accelerating and margins are improving. However, part of the revenue jump is low-margin Mumbai distribution pass-through, and earlier-period figures are internally inconsistent (9M FY26 revenue exceeds full-year FY26). On the capital-intensive yardstick the sector card favours, EV/EBITDA of 25.1x is far above what regulated utility annuities typically command, and P/B of 7.2x against ROE of only 9.7% plus a trailing P/E of 81.7x (P88 vs the broad market) make the stock expensive even after allowing for strong growth, rising sell-side estimates (FY EPS +16% over 30 days) and the price sitting near its 52-week high (89.5% of range). The biggest risk is the balance sheet: net debt of about ₹49,156 cr (6.2x FY26 EBITDA), negative free cash flow (H1 FCF of -₹3,185 cr, with ₹21–25k cr of annual capex guided), and Adani-group governance risk leave little room for error if execution slips or interest rates stay high.

Adani Total Gas is a city gas distributor selling CNG to vehicles and piped gas to homes and industry, a regulated volume business that is closer to a utility than to an oil company. In the latest quarter with official filings (Q1FY27; the Q2FY27 results PDF filed 2026-10-22 has not yet been extracted), revenue grew +27.2% YoY to ₹1,907 cr, faster than the roughly +17–21% of FY26, but PAT fell -14.2% to ₹142 cr. PAT margin compressed from 11.0% in Q1FY26 to 7.4%, and EBITDA margin dropped from about 19–20% to 11.2%, so the company is selling more gas but keeping much less of each rupee, which points to higher gas sourcing costs not being passed on to customers. On EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for this capital-intensive business, the stock trades at 58.9× against a 23.3× median (P93, though the comparison set is the broad market, not tight peers), and trailing P/E of 105× is far above the 10–18× Utilities and 8–14× Energy ranges, so it is expensive even at 33% of its 52-week range. On valuation I used EV/EBITDA plus peer rank, not the card's 9-12x mobile-telecom band: 15.3x EV/EBITDA (P27 vs a broad-market median of 23.3x) and 32.6x trailing P/E (P46, near the median) grade it fair, and the forward P/E of 21.6x assumes an earnings recovery that the falling sell-side estimates (-3% over 90 days, 2 of 2 analysts at sell) do not yet support. The biggest risk is cash conversion: H1 operating cash flow was -₹42 cr and free cash flow -₹202 cr, so growth is being bought with working capital and capex rather than producing cash.

rules.eligible: growth == strong, risk != high, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (newest results period's YoY revenue growth >= the preceding period's, from the filing extracts; a missing number passes)
rules.rank: revenue acceleration (highest first), then revenue growth, then symbol
rules.entry: next open, once the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions; slots freed by sells are refilled from the eligible list the same session
rules.hold: re-judged every session on the latest view (refreshed on each results filing); topped up toward target when below 75% of target and cash allows (anti-chase applies; entries are funded first); re-qualification review every 120 sessions since entry (then since the last review): must still pass growth == strong, risk != high, revenue growth not decelerating (a missing number passes), else sold — a name failing the gate but not deteriorated is sold only at this review, never earlier
rules.exit: growth -> weak, risk -> high, sentiment bearish with conviction >= 0.5, or the 120-session review failing (growth not strong, risk high or decelerating); between reviews never for decelerating, never for timing, never on missing data

rules.rank: growth grade (strong first), then conviction, then symbol
rules.entry: next open; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions (no results-timing leg); slots freed by sells are refilled the same session
rules.hold: re-judged every session on the latest view (refreshed on each results filing); topped up toward target when below 75% of target and cash allows (anti-chase applies; entries are funded first); re-qualification review every 120 sessions since entry (then since the last review): must still pass growth in {strong, moderate}, risk != high, conviction >= 0.5 (rule (a) without the data-quality leg), else sold — a name failing the gate but not deteriorated is sold only at this review, never earlier
rules.exit: growth -> weak, risk -> high, sentiment bearish with conviction >= 0.5, or the 120-session review failing (rule (a) no longer met); between reviews never for decelerating, never for timing, never on missing data
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); this book trims on the flip down and tops up any session
rules.review_gate: growth in {strong, moderate}, risk != high, conviction >= 0.5

books.title: Book 6 bottom-up, neutral tilts (no model)
books.hypothesis: Book 6's construction with every sector tilt at 1.0, run live beside Book 6: the line the model tilt must beat by more than the random band (the bounds study of 26 Oct 2026 found no pack field beat it; the TWR line cannot judge the tilt, Book 6 − b6_neutral and the sector-call scorecard can).

rules.signal: monthly signal date recorded (rebalance cadence); NO sector_strategist call
rules.tilt: 1.0 for every sector, always (neutral = equal share over the sectors with eligible names or a holding)
rules.eligible: the shared fundamental filter: growth == strong, risk != high, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (newest results period's YoY revenue growth >= the preceding period's, from the filing extracts; a missing number passes); ranked by revenue acceleration (highest first), then revenue growth, then symbol
rules.slots: 30 slots apportioned over the active sectors by largest remainder on w_s x 30 (sum = 30 exactly), with hysteresis: a sector's count changes only when its exact share moves > 0.5 slot from its current allocation; weight w_s / k_s each, capped at 2/30
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); rebalanced on the monthly signal date and on the flip
rules.entry: next open, once the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions or exited in the last 20 sessions
rules.exit: fundamental deterioration (growth -> weak / risk -> high), or a tilt cut dropping k_s below the names held (lowest-ranked sold first); never on missing data, decelerating growth or timing
rules.rebalance: signal dates and the session the overlay flips; survivors outside +/-25% of target
rules.attribution: monthly Brinson vs the equal-weight universe (leaderboard key b6_neutral_attribution); no sector calls, so no scorecard
rules.judge: the comparator for Book 6: Book 6 − b6_neutral is the tilt's contribution

books.title: Growth screen (ranked by PAT growth)
books.hypothesis: Avoid what the grades call losers (high risk, weak growth, poor data, decelerating), then buy the highest reported revenue growth — the one fundamental the winners forensic found on the winners' side — with Book 3's construction.

rules.eligible: risk != high, growth != weak, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (a missing number passes), revenue growth YoY > 0 (newest results period with a number; missing fails)
rules.rank: PAT growth YoY from the filings, highest first (missing last), then revenue growth, then symbol
rules.entry: next open, once the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions; slots freed by sells are refilled from the eligible list the same session
rules.hold: re-judged every session on the latest view (refreshed on each results filing); topped up toward target when below 75% of target and cash allows (anti-chase applies; entries are funded first); re-qualification review every 120 sessions since entry (then since the last review): must still pass the same filter, else sold — a name failing the gate but not deteriorated is sold only at this review, never earlier
rules.exit: growth -> weak, risk -> high, or the 120-session review failing (the same filter); no sentiment exit
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); this book trims on the flip down and tops up any session
rules.review_gate: risk != high, growth != weak, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (a missing number passes), revenue growth YoY > 0 (newest results period with a number; missing fails)

books.kill_rule: more than 10 points behind the equal-weight null on a rolling 60-date basis, twice in a row
books.promote_rule: best book at 90 dates, if ahead of both benchmarks

brinson.method: Brinson-Fachler vs the equal-weight universe, start-of-month holdings held through the month; Cash is a sector with zero return and zero benchmark weight
